hypothesis: A completed-bar trailing exit activated only after HYPE extends beyond its eight-hour soft boundary may retain more profit than either the unrestricted extension or a fixed eight-hour exit.
decision: Continue the frozen 20, 30, and 40 bps post-soft trails as report-only observers. Do not activate a trail from two resolved long-side counterfactuals. Keep this hypothesis explicitly separate from the staged fixed-eight-hour candidate because a fixed exit prevents a post-soft trail from operating.
falsifier: Reject the post-soft trail hypothesis if new profile-matched extensions fail to beat fixed eight hours after costs. Promote only after one frozen policy repeatedly beats the fixed boundary per lifecycle across long and short extensions with measured venue friction; changed source-prefix hashes would invalidate the current audit.
limitations: Only two extension lifecycles are resolved and both are long.
The fixed-boundary and trail exits are counterfactual estimates, not submitted orders.
Completed one-minute extrema cannot reconstruct intraminute trigger ordering.
The 20 bps aggregate advantage is concentrated in one of two lifecycles.
The current open HYPE lifecycle had not reached its soft deadline at the evidence boundary.
